title: Inverting a lift of a unit modulo I is etale and does not change A/I
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $a\in A$ an element whose image $\bar a$ in $A/I$ is a unit. Let $A_a$ be the localization of $A$ at $\{1,a,a^2,\dots\}$. Then (1) $\operatorname{Spec}A_a\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]; (2) the map $\alpha:A/I\to A_a/IA_a$ induced by $A\to A_a$ is an isomorphism; (3) the image $u=a/1$ of $a$ in $A_a$ is a unit of $A_a$, and its image in $A_a/IA_a$ is $\alpha(\bar a)$. In particular (Stacks 07LX): for every unit $\bar u$ of $A/I$ there is a ring map $A\to A'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale, $A/I\to A'/IA'$ an isomorphism $\alpha$, and a unit $u'\in A'$ whose image in $A'/IA'$ is $\alpha(\bar u)$ (take $a$ any lift of $\bar u$, $A'=A_a$).
